evidence: The A page declares qm-framework-and-quantities in its requires list (manifest and library carrier agree). The consumed content is the state postulate P1 homed there and the framework vocabulary: the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space, pure preparations as unit rays, general preparations as density operators, and the zero-vector exclusion, which this page only reads in geometry vocabulary and never restates as a second postulate.

Adopted as formulation prerequisite in clause (a): the definition states that it adopts the state postulate for a declared system with its assigned Hilbert space H and fixes the readings of its clauses (i)-(iii) as the state space D(H), state, pure/mixed state and purity. No physical assumption is added beyond the postulate's own clauses, and the bijection from unit rays to pure states of clause (b) cites clause (ii) of the postulate.

The statement adopts P1 and proves conditional consequences: fact [F1] restates clauses (i)-(iii) (assigned Hilbert space; unit rays as pure preparations, equal up to a nonzero complex factor; density operators as general preparations; zero vector excluded), and clause (c) of the item uses the postulate's zero-vector exclusion at steps 3.1. The theorem asserts nothing beyond the postulate together with the batch-local mathematics.

The statement adopts P1; clause (a) is the mixture clause of P1 (clause (iii)) read through the batch-local convexity lemma, fact [F1]/[F2] fix the preparation and mixture vocabulary from the postulate, and clause (c) with step 2.1 concludes that a mixed preparation is a nontrivial mixture of two preparations. The mixture weights are the postulate's classical preparation probabilities.

Fact [L1] cites clauses (ii)-(iii) of the state postulate verbatim in content (pure preparation a unit ray; rank-one density operator attached to a unit vector's ray; zero vector not a state; general preparation of trace one), and steps 1.1-2.2 use it to refute the claim that the zero vector determines a pure preparation with the zero operator as its state.

Part 1 of the remark records that the model assumption (assigned Hilbert space, pure preparations as unit rays, general preparations as density operators) is clause-level content of the postulate homed on the framework page, that this page does not restate it, and that its two physics theorems are conditional consequences of it. The remark proves nothing and adds no assumption.

The example's starting data are the model's two-level finite-spin assignment: the internal space H = C^2 of a spin-one-half system with the standard inner product, which is exactly the clause of P6 adopted on the framework page. The Bloch-ball computation is conditional on that assignment and asserts no interpretation of r beyond the displayed formula.

Fact [L1] cites clause (e) of the proposition for the Pauli algebra used throughout: sigma_i^2 = I, the anticommutation and product rules sigma_i sigma_j = delta_ij I + i sum_k eps_ijk sigma_k, hermiticity and vanishing trace. The eigenvalues 1 +/- |r| of (I + r.sigma)/2 and the rank-one boundary computation at steps 2.2 and 3.1 use these identities.

Clause (a) of the lemma is cited for the definition of density operator (self-adjoint positive trace class with trace one) as the content of the model's general-preparation class, and the spectral expansion of clause (a) is the basis for the item's pure/mixed classification by positive eigenvalues.

The rank-one operators T_{u,u} of the calculus are cited for the candidate pure states: the definition uses T_{x,y}z = <z,y>x and its trace/positivity properties to state that the pure states are the operators T_{u,u} with u in the unit sphere, cross-checked against the batch-local ray-to-state lemma.

Fact [F2] cites clause (a) of the lemma for the membership characterization of D(H) used in every step: rho self-adjoint, positive and trace class with trace one; the convexity, trace-norm completeness and boundedness conclusions are proved from that characterization together with the cited trace-class ideal theorems.

Fact [F1] cites clause (a) of the lemma for the density-operator characterization and the spectral expansion rho = sum_n lambda_n T_{u_n,u_n} with lambda_n >= 0 summing to one; the criterion tr(rho^2) = 1 iff pure is proved from this expansion by summing the squared weights.

Fact [F3] cites clause (a) of the lemma for the spectral expansion of a state (rho = sum_n lambda_n T_{u_n,u_n}, positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity) used in step 4.1 to split any non-pure state into a nontrivial convex combination, and the positivity/trace-one characterization enters through the batch-local density-set lemma.

Fact [F1] cites the full rank-one calculus: boundedness with norm product, linearity in the first and conjugate-linearity in the second variable, trace-class membership with trace-norm |u||v| and trace <u,v>, adjoint and positivity properties, composition rules, and trace-norm continuity. Steps 1.1, 2.1, 2.2 and 4.1 use exactly these clauses for scaling, projection identification, equality criteria and well-definedness of the ray-to-state map.

Fact [F3] cites clause (a) of the lemma for the spectral expansion of every density operator (weights lambda_n >= 0 summing to one over an orthonormal eigenfamily, weights the positive eigenvalues with multiplicity); step 1.2 turns this expansion into the countable mixture of pairwise orthogonal pure preparations of clause (b).

Fact [L3] cites the calculus for T_{0,v} = 0 and tr(T_{0,0}) = <0,0> = 0; step 2.2 uses these values to show the zero operator is not a density operator, completing the refutation that the zero vector determines a preparation.
